substantive_delta: The exact frozen upper theorem gives n*3^n vertex-update memory per player, preserves the entire payoff of any given pure SPE, and covers every set-sized arbitrarily branching arena and every legal history. This removes arena dependence from the finite-arena baseline and applies beyond absorbing-leaf uniformization. The Flesch existence application is routine, and the lower-bound family is supporting evidence rather than independent qualitative novelty.
why_nonroutine: The old lasso and play-following constructions do not themselves yield a finite memory bound independent of the graph. Nor can a completed payoff promise be replaced by an absorbing leaf: unsatisfied players retain legal future deviations. The audited compatibility-retention and previous-owner reset rule, coupled to finite-target progress, resolves both obligations with an explicit vertex-update machine and an invariant for arbitrary unilateral deviations. Labels, positional path selection and minimizing punishments are credited as antecedents; the accepted innovation is their full-scope continuing-arena uniformization.
significance: This settles the stated arena-independent constrained-SPE question, and additionally proves unconditional pure finite-memory existence on arbitrary arenas using an old existence theorem. Together with the verified all-SPE singleton-required-winner lower bound it determines exponential-order dependence on player count. This is substantive specialized mathematical value; broad STOC impact and technical depth remain uncertain, as the separate working_paper assessment explains.
